subject: Q4 Renewal Sprint: Aligning multi-year ramp and burst onboarding
messages:
From: Tess Lewis <tess.lewis@stratushealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@stratushealth.com>
Date: 2028-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal notice — upcoming term options and potential burst capacity

Hi Lukas,

We're starting to plan our renewal for the account (term ends 2029-01-31) and there are three things we'd like to explore: a multi-year commitment with a front-loaded ramp for the first 6 months, the option to add quarter-burst capacity during high-demand windows, and co-terming to our fiscal year (FYQ1).

Can your team outline the typical structures you recommend for a case like ours (mix of committed + burst), and what the procurement/legal asks tend to be for an auto-renew clause? We're also evaluating payment cadence (annual vs. quarterly).

CC'd procurement — Nadia, can you confirm what information you need from Redwood to get an internal PO routed?

Thanks,
Tess
Tess Lewis
Director, Platform Ops
Stratus Health

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tess Lewis <tess.lewis@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@stratushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-20T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal notice — upcoming term options and potential burst capacity

Hi Tess — thanks for the heads up. High level answers below, I'll loop in the team to put together a short proposal you can share with procurement: 

- Typical structures: 1) Multi-year committed with a graded ramp (e.g., 50% first quarter, 25% second, 25% thereafter), 2) Annual commit + on-demand quarter-burst blocks, 3) Hybrid: committed baseline + pre-purchased burst credits that expire at co-term.
- Auto-renew: common to include an opt-out window (30–60 days) and a true-up clause tied to usage at year-end. Procurement sometimes asks for a maximum annual increase cap or formal notice period.
- Billing: annual prepay gives best unit economics; quarterly invoicing is fine with a small surcharge.

Marissa/karthik — can you draft two alternatives (24-month with front-loaded ramp, and 12-month with burst credits) and attach a ramp table? Monica/Neha — any operational constraints we should surface (onboarding timeline, ramp support days, projected SLOs during bursts)?

Tess/Nadia — we'll aim to have a digest you can circulate to procurement by EOD 10/22.

Best,
Lukas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Q4 Renewal Sprint: Aligning multi-year ramp and burst onboarding

Team — draft attached. Key points: 24-month multi-year option and 12-month hybrid option.

Summary (see Annex-A_ramp_table.xlsx):
- Option A (24m, front-loaded): 40% commit in months 1–3 (to cover migration/burst onboarding), then linear ramp to full committed baseline by month 7. Auto-renew every 12 months with 45-day opt-out. Yearly true-up aligned to calendar year if co-term not accepted.
- Option B (12m hybrid): 100% baseline at a lower commit + purchasable burst blocks (100k token blocks) that expire at co-term. Auto-renew with 30-day opt-out and usage true-up quarterly.

Operational notes from Monica: we can support burst onboarding in two 4-week sprints (engineering + onboarding runs) to ensure KV cache priming and latency SLOs. Need a mutually agreed window for pre-bought burst activation (48–72 hours notice).

Finance note from Neha: annual prepay reduces unit price by ~12% vs quarterly invoicing. For co-terming to FYQ1 we can prorate the first partial period to align start date without penalizing the customer — recommend a short bridge credit for the fractional months.

Attachments: Annex-A_ramp_table.xlsx (ramp cadence + pricing samples), Renewal_Summary_Stratus_2028.pdf (one-pager).

Marissa
Sr. Renewals Manager

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tess Lewis <tess.lewis@stratushealth.com>, Nadia Bowers <nbowers@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-22T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: 24-month front-loaded ramp + co-terming bridge (Stratus Health)

Hi Tess/Nadia — attaching a short proposal and a ramp table for your review. TL;DR: we recommend Option A (24-month front-loaded ramp) if Stratus wants to minimize disruption during the migration to the new service patterns and ensure capacity during the first two quarters. Key operational commitments below: 

- Ramp: 40% capacity allocated months 1–3 for migration; full baseline achieved by end of month 7.
- Burst: pre-purchased burst blocks available in 100k token increments. Activation requires 48–72 hours notice for the first activation; subsequent activations can be reduced to 24 hours with a runbook sign-off.
- Co-term: we can co-term to your FYQ1 start date; Redwood will provide a prorated bridge credit for the partial period to align to the fiscal boundary.
- Auto-renew: 45-day opt-out window; yearly true-up tied to baseline vs. measured usage; maximum annual price increase capped at 7% in contract (we accepted that to help procurement).

Next steps: please confirm 1) preferred option (A or B), 2) desired co-term date, and 3) procurement contact for DocuSign. If you confirm Option A, we'll prepare a redline-friendly DocuSign packet and estimate for signatures.

Attachments: Renewal_Summary_Stratus_2028.pdf, Annex-A_ramp_table.xlsx

Thanks,
Lukas

Date: 2028-10-24T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 24-month front-loaded ramp + co-terming bridge (Stratus Health)

Hi Lukas/Tess — procurement reviewed the summary. A few asks before we can route a PO: 

1) Can you shorten the auto-renew opt-out window to 30 days? Our procurement policy prefers 30 days for enterprise vendors.
2) We need true-up timing to be quarterly rather than annual for our internal chargeback process. Quarterly true-ups are acceptable if the contract includes a small reconciliation fee (<1% of quarterly spend) for shortfalls.
3) Please provide a DocuSign packet with a clear PO line for 'burst credits' and an MOP section (we prefer ACH; need bank details + W9).

If you can accept 1) and 2) we'll move forward quickly.

Thanks,
Nadia Bowers
Sr. Procurement Manager
Stratus Health
